Mehrauli Archaeological Park

A guided heritage walk through ten centuries of building, from the Sultanate to the British period

On request

Arranged for your group. Send your preferred dates, group size and location. We adapt the length, level and language, and prepare a quotation. The suggested group size is a guide, not a requirement.

Request on WhatsApp Request by email

No payment is taken until you approve the plan. Common questions

The park holds standing remains from the eleventh century to the nineteenth, among them Rajon ki Baoli, the tomb of Balban and the mosque and tomb of Jamali Kamali. An archaeologist shows how masonry, arches and decoration distinguish one period from the next.

The date, start time, pace and language are arranged to suit your group.

What it covers

  • Rajon ki Baoli, a Lodi-period stepwell with its mosque and tomb
  • Balban's tomb, with one of the earliest true arches in India
  • The mosque and tomb of Jamali Kamali, from the first years of Mughal rule
  • Quli Khan's tomb, which a British official turned into a country house

How the time is spent

  1. Orientation: Mehrauli landscape 25 min

    Use a layered map to place the park amid historic Delhi cities.

    You: mark a chronology

  2. Balban tomb precinct 55 min

    Contrast surviving masonry, arches and architectural claims.

    You: sketch an arch

  3. Jamali Kamali exterior/precinct 55 min

    Discuss early Mughal form, inscriptions and conservation.

    You: compare ornament

  4. Rajon ki Baoli and Quli Khan area 25 min

    Trace water, gardens and later adaptive reuse from accessible areas.

    You: annotate a site map

Timings are a guide. The plan is confirmed with your quotation.

By the end you can

  • Identify and interpret key features of Mehrauli Archaeological Park using material evidence and a site map.
  • Read Delhi's layers through tombs, baolis and reused buildings.
  • Distinguish directly visible fabric from reconstructed or debated historical claims.

You take away

Your annotated field card, sketches and notes.
